channel.title: Georgia Public Broadcasting - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Georgia Public Broadcasting (gpb.org)

item.title: Supreme Court appears skeptical of laws counting mail-in ballots after Election Day
item.description: The Supreme Court heard arguments in a case that tests whether states should be allowed to count ballots that are mailed on time but arrive after Election Day. The case could have broad implications.

item.title: Trump delivers farmers another financial blow with Iran war
item.description: Some of President Trump's policies, the latest being the war in Iran, are testing his support among farmers who are being burdened with higher costs.

item.title: Lawmakers: Spotlight - Georgia Budget Explained: Tax Cuts, Surplus Spending, &amp; What It Means for You
item.description: Georgia lawmakers break down the state’s amended and upcoming budgets, explaining how billions in tax revenue are allocated and what proposed income tax cuts could mean for your wallet. You’ll hear how education, mental health, and property tax relief are shaping spending priorities, along with insights into surplus funds and economic pressures. This episode helps you understand how state budget decisions directly impact your daily life in Georgia.

item.title: Pakistan is poised to host the U.S. and Iran for talks to end the war
item.description: The Pakistani prime minister said his country stands ready to host negotiations toward a settlement as the war with Iran nears the one-month mark.

item.title: Judge, expressing doubt on abortion murder charge, grants bond to Georgia mother
item.description: A Coastal Georgia district attorney and a Superior Court judge said Monday they were doubtful that enough evidence exists to move forward with a malice murder charge against a 31-year-old Camden County mother arrested earlier this month for an alleged illegal abortion, paving the way for a possible reduction or dismissal of charges.

item.title: Georgia is one of the first states with a law protecting people seeking senior living communities
item.description: Selecting an appropriate senior living option for a loved one can be a confusing process, especially when it comes to referral agencies. Senate Bill 439 establishes standards so that families understand what options are being presented and when financial interests are involved.

item.title: GPB morning headlines for March 25, 2026
item.description: Atlanta-based Delta Air Lines is suspending its special services for members of Congress as the partial shutdown continues to cause long lines at airports nationwide; a Georgia Senate committee passed a bill creating a homelessness prevention program Tuesday.

item.title: Georgia could become the first state with weapons detection in all public schools
item.description: Georgia lawmakers may require that every public school student be checked for weapons each day. On Monday, a Senate committee advanced a bill, pushing it closer to final passage.

item.title: A 92-year-old judge will take on the Maduro case. What do we know about him?
item.description: Former Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro heads to court again this week. The judge overseeing this case is longtime federal Judge Alvin Hellerstein. At 92 years old, Hellerstein is older than the average age of a federal judge by more than 20 years.

item.title: Belgian drugmaker UCB to invest $2B in suburban Atlanta plant, adding 330 jobs
item.description: Belgian pharmaceutical maker UCB says it will build a $2 billion drug manufacturing plant near Atlanta.

item.title: DHS funding deal on shaky ground as Trump and Democrats both decline to embrace it
item.description: After weeks of start and stop negotiations between Congressional Democrats and the White House, there's an emerging proposal to fund the majority of DHS and tackle ICE enforcement funding separately.

item.title: 'We're all in grief': Chicano artists reckon with Cesar Chavez abuse allegations
item.description: Artists, filmmakers and singers once championed Chavez as a hero. Now, they must rethink how to tell his story. "It's just been gut-wrenching," one muralist says.

item.title: Iran rejects Trump's proposal to end the war and lays out 5 conditions, state TV says
item.description: Iran submitted a counterproposal that includes safeguards against future attacks against Iran and the country's right to "sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz," Iranian state Press TV reported.

item.title: A leadership vacuum adds to strains on the CDC
item.description: Low morale, staff turnover and budget issues have sapped the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The administration is expected to soon name a new director, who will have their hands full.

item.title: At the Legacy Museum, facing America's racist past is a path, not a punishment
item.description: "There is an America that is more free — where there's more equality, where there is more justice, where there is less bigotry — and I think it's waiting for us," says lawyer Bryan Stevenson.
